findings.title: No upgrade path adds the Clients resource type and its scopes to already-initialized admin-permissions resource servers
findings.body: init() bootstraps the admin-permissions resource server (all schema scopes plus one 'all' resource per resource type) only when the realm's admin permissions client is first created; it returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions v2 before this change have a resource server containing only the Users scopes (manage, view, impersonate, map-roles, manage-group-membership) and no 'Clients' resource, and nothing in this PR ever updates them. On such realms: creating a Clients permission fails (getOrCreateResource throws ModelException("No scopes found.") because scopeStore.findByName returns null for the new scopes configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite, and getScope rejects them as not existing); all-clients evaluation in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String) always returns false because findByName(server, "Clients") returns null; and per-client evaluation can hit a NullPointerException in ClientPermissionsV2's fallback. A migration/upgrade step that adds the missing scopes and the Clients all-resource to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed, otherwise the new feature is broken (with 500s) for every realm that adopted v2 earlier.

findings.title: Missing null check on the 'Clients' all-resource leads to NullPointerException in per-client permission checks
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking the result. getResourceTypeResource can return null — it does so whenever the 'Clients' resource is absent from the resource server (e.g., realms whose admin permissions client was initialized before the Clients type was added to the schema, since init() never runs again for them) or when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false. findByResource then dereferences resource.getId() and throws a NullPointerException, so every per-client permission check (canView/canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles for a specific client) performed by a delegated admin returns a 500 instead of denying or granting access. Guard the null (return false) and/or ensure the resource is created on upgrade.

findings.title: Deleting a client fails when both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled
findings.body: The removal listener added here is guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (v1), but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the v2 feature flag is on, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. If an operator enables both the v1 and v2 features, handling ClientRemovedEvent calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which resolves to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Provider event listener exceptions propagate, so every client deletion in the realm fails with an error and the transaction rolls back. The guard needs to select the cleanup path based on which evaluator is actually active (or ClientPermissionsV2 must implement a no-op/real cleanup) instead of only checking the v1 flag.

findings.title: No cleanup of FGAP v2 client resources and permissions when a client is deleted
findings.body: setPermissionsEnabled here throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the AdminPermissions.registerListener cleanup hook that used to invoke it on ClientRemovedEvent is now skipped whenever the v1 feature flag is off — i.e., in the standard v2-only setup. As a result, deleting a client that has fine-grained permissions leaves the resource created for it in the admin-permissions resource server (named by the client's internal id, created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource when a permission targets that client) and all permissions referencing it orphaned. These stale entries remain visible in permission listings and are still returned by getClientsWithPermission, so callers that resolve the returned names via session.clients().getClientById get nulls for deleted clients. A v2 cleanup path for client removal (deleting the resource and its referencing permissions) is missing.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName resolves friendly resource names only for the Users type (returning the username, or "All users" for the all-resource). Resources of the newly added Clients type fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for resources created by getOrCreateResource, so REST/admin-console representations of client permissions will render an empty or null name instead of the client's clientId, and the 'Clients' all-resource gets no equivalent of the "All users" label. Mirror the Users branch for CLIENTS: return "All clients" for the all-resource and resolve the client via session.clients().getClientById(realm, resource.getName()) to return its clientId.
